finding.claim: A user-supplied callbackUrl is stored with no validation. notifyAll later sends a POST to it from the server. An attacker can point it at internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (for example http://169.254.169.254/), or localhost. This is stored SSRF. The POST body is the job payload, and the status code and error behaviour can give the attacker feedback.
finding.sink: HttpClient.send on a request built with URI.create(cb) (Jobs.java:20-24)

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL
URL stored in the subscriptions map without any checks
notifyAll iterates the stored callback URLs
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen host

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check (http, https, file etc.), no host allowlist, no private, loopback or link-local IP block, no DNS-rebinding protection, and no authentication or authorization on subscribe is visible in this file. The default HttpClient does not follow redirects, which limits redirect-based pivoting but does not stop direct requests to internal hosts.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:13-14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and notifyAll (Jobs.java:19-24) builds URI.create(cb) and calls client.send with no scheme, host or IP check anywhere in the codebase (the only regex guard is on the separate thumb() at line 30). Note the claim that the POST body is the job payload is accurate (line 22), the "authentication on subscribe" absence cannot be fully verified because no handler/middleware code exists in the repo, and the default HttpClient does not follow redirects, which does not stop direct internal requests.
